title: Iran war: 'I might have gone too far' vs 'we can do that in 10 minutes'

before.quote: I might have gone too far.
before.where: Campaign rally, Bullhead City, Arizona

after.quote: But we can do that in, in 10 minutes. 10 minutes.
after.where: Press gaggle at a Halloween party, Mar-a-Lago, Palm Beach, Florida

context: At a rally in Bullhead City, Arizona, Trump said he might have gone too far in the Iran war because, with so many Iranian leaders killed, he no longer knew whom to negotiate with. Seventeen days later, at a press gaggle at Mar-a-Lago, he said talks with Iran were going fine but that the other side was not very reliable, and that one or two remaining nuclear sites could be dealt with in 10 minutes, adding that a plan for it exists (the transcript's strike passage follows a question about the Qatari-mediated talks). Also on October 31, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Trump had not decided whether to resume strikes and prefers a diplomatic resolution. The two statements are not strictly incompatible: doubts about how far a campaign went and readiness to resume targeted strikes can coexist. The pair is listed because the same speaker described the scale of the war as possibly excessive and, two weeks later, presented further strikes as quick and already planned. The rally article places the speech on a Wednesday, which gives October 14; the exact date is inferred from that.

moreSources.label: Fox News — Iran live updates, Oct 31 (Rubio: no decision on resuming strikes)
Global News — 'Trump says he "might have gone too far" in war on Iran' (Oct 14 listing)

title: Iran war: Trump sought allied help, then said 'WE NEVER DID' need it

before.quote: Many countries ... will be sending warships ... to keep the Strait of Hormuz open and safe.
before.where: Truth Social statement calling for international assistance securing the Strait of Hormuz

after.quote: We no longer 'need,' or desire, the NATO Countries' assistance — WE NEVER DID!
after.where: Truth Social post after NATO allies declined to join the operation

context: During the March 2026 Iran war, Trump publicly called for other countries to help protect shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. After NATO allies declined involvement, he claimed the United States never needed their help. On March 17 he also said in the Oval Office, 'we don't need them, but they should have been there.' This is a documented reversal in his public description of whether allied help was needed; asking for help and later saying it was not strictly necessary are not inherently logically incompatible.

title: WikiLeaks: from 'I love' to 'I know nothing'

before.quote: I love WikiLeaks!
before.where: Campaign rally, Wilkes-Barre, Pennsylvania

after.quote: I know nothing about WikiLeaks. It's not my thing.
after.where: Oval Office, White House, Washington, D.C.

context: Trump enthusiastically praised WikiLeaks during the 2016 campaign, then distanced himself from the organization following Julian Assange's arrest in 2019. The contrast is documented in contemporaneous reporting and an official presidential transcript.

title: NATO: 'obsolete' in 2016, 'no longer obsolete' in 2017

before.quote: I think NATO's obsolete.
before.where: ABC This Week interview

after.quote: I said it was obsolete. It's no longer obsolete.
after.where: White House joint press conference with NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg

context: Trump publicly reversed his characterization of NATO, citing changes in the alliance's focus on counterterrorism. This is an acknowledged policy assessment change, not necessarily evidence of deception.

before.where: Twitter post urging President Obama not to intervene militarily

after.quote: Tonight, I ordered a targeted military strike on the airfield in Syria.

title: Unemployment statistics: 'hoax' before inauguration, embraced afterward

before.quote: One of the biggest hoaxes in modern American politics.
before.where: Economic Club of Detroit speech, referring to the official unemployment rate

after.quote: They may have been phony in the past, but it's very real now.
after.where: White House press briefing; Sean Spicer quoting Trump's response to the new jobs report

context: Trump questioned the credibility of official unemployment figures before taking office, then celebrated the same statistical series. The second quotation was relayed by his press secretary rather than spoken directly on camera.

title: Medicaid: 'without cuts' vs backing reduced federal spending

before.quote: Save Medicare, Medicaid and Social Security without cuts.
before.where: Presidential campaign announcement, Trump Tower, New York City

after.quote: Backed the House Republican American Health Care Act, which proposed major reductions to projected federal Medicaid spending.
after.where: White House support for House Republican health-care proposal (action, not verbatim quote)

context: This is a promise-versus-policy comparison. The later item is a documented action, not a direct Trump quotation; the proposal capped federal Medicaid growth. It does not mean all Medicaid beneficiaries would immediately lose coverage.

title: Stock market: 'big, fat, ugly bubble' vs celebrating gains

before.quote: We are in a big, fat, ugly bubble.
before.where: First presidential debate, Hofstra University, New York

after.quote: Trillions of dollars of value have been created since I won the election.
after.where: Fox & Friends interview

context: Trump criticized stock-market gains under Obama as an artificial bubble but cited stock-market gains after his election as a positive economic indicator. A changed market assessment is not by itself a factual contradiction.

title: Tax returns: 'it'll be released' versus continued refusal

before.quote: I don't mind releasing. I'm under a routine audit, and it'll be released.
before.where: First presidential debate, Hofstra University, Hempstead, New York

after.quote: I'm not releasing the tax returns because, as you know, they're under audit.
after.where: Press conference, Trump Tower, New York City

context: The 2016 statement suggested release after an audit; in 2017 Trump continued withholding the returns on audit grounds. An audit does not legally prevent voluntary publication. This is a change in stated willingness, not evidence of a legal obligation.

title: Putin: 'got to know him very well' vs 'no relationship'

before.quote: I got to know him very well because we were both on 60 Minutes.
before.where: Republican presidential debate

after.quote: I have no relationship with Putin.
after.where: ABC This Week interview with George Stephanopoulos

context: Trump described a personal connection to Putin in 2015, then denied any relationship in 2016. The 60 Minutes interviews were recorded separately, a relevant distinction. PolitiFact rated the change a Full Flop.

title: Abortion: punish women — then not women

before.where: MSNBC town hall with Chris Matthews, Green Bay, Wisconsin

after.quote: The doctor or any other person performing this illegal act upon a woman would be held legally responsible, not the woman.

context: In the town hall, Trump answered yes when pressed on punishment for women; later the same day, his campaign stated that women would not be punished. This is a same-day reversal, not a claim about current law.

title: Planned Parenthood: defund it, then keep some funding

before.quote: Absolutely, they should be defunded.
before.where: Blaze TV interview

after.quote: I'd look at the good aspects of it, and I would also look because I'm against abortion.

context: Trump first called for defunding Planned Parenthood, then discussed preserving support for its non-abortion health services. His position changed again in September. The precise distinction between funding the organization and specific services matters.

title: Birtherism: 'birth certificate is a fraud' vs 'born in the United States'

before.quote: An 'extremely credible source' has called my office and told me that @BarackObama's birth certificate is a fraud.
before.where: Twitter post

after.quote: President Barack Obama was born in the United States, period.
after.where: Statement at the Trump International Hotel, Washington, D.C.

context: Trump questioned President Obama's birthplace for years, including a 2012 tweet calling the birth certificate a fraud, then acknowledged in September 2016 that Obama was born in the United States. In the same statement he blamed Hillary Clinton's 2008 campaign for starting the controversy; FactCheck.org found no evidence of that (see the separate entry).

title: Iraq war: 'Yeah, I guess so' vs 'totally against'

before.quote: Yeah, I guess so.
before.where: Howard Stern radio interview, answering whether he supported invading Iraq

after.quote: I was totally against the war in Iraq.
after.where: NBC News Commander-in-Chief Forum, New York

context: FactCheck.org found no evidence that Trump opposed the war before the March 19, 2003 invasion; he voiced concerns about its cost and direction a few months after it began. PolitiFact rated his 2016 claim False. The 2002 answer responded to a question about a not-yet-launched invasion, which is why the sourced timeline matters.

title: Stormy Daniels payment: 'No. No.' then 'through reimbursement'

before.quote: No. No. What else?
before.where: Air Force One, answering whether he knew about the $130,000 payment

after.quote: …received a monthly retainer, not from the campaign… through reimbursement…
after.where: Tweets acknowledging that Michael Cohen was reimbursed (excerpt)

context: On April 5, 2018 Trump said no when asked whether he knew about the $130,000 payment to Stormy Daniels, and said to ask his attorney Michael Cohen. On May 3 he acknowledged that Cohen had been reimbursed, while saying campaign money played no role in the transaction. On whether the April 5 denial misled the public, FactCheck.org wrote 'It would appear so.'

title: Comey firing: 'this Russia thing' vs 'never fired … because of Russia'

before.quote: this Russia thing with Trump and Russia is a made up story
before.where: NBC News interview with Lester Holt, White House, explaining his decision to fire James Comey

after.quote: Not that it matters but I never fired James Comey because of Russia!
after.where: Twitter post

context: In May 2017 Trump told NBC News that when he decided to fire Comey he regarded the Russia matter as a made-up story, even though a memo by Deputy Attorney General Rod Rosenstein, which did not mention the Russia inquiry, had been presented as the rationale. In May 2018 he tweeted that Russia was not the reason. Whether Russia was a motive is a separate legal question; this entry only documents that his two public accounts differ.

title: COVID-19: 'I wanted to always play it down' vs 'I didn't lie'

before.quote: I wanted to always play it down.
before.where: Recorded call with journalist Bob Woodward (made public in September 2020)

after.quote: I didn't lie.
after.where: Remarks reported by NBC News

context: In recorded calls with Woodward, Trump said in February 2020 the virus was more deadly than a strenuous flu and in March that he wanted to always play it down. In public he continued to say the virus was like a flu. After the recordings emerged he said he had not lied and that the message was to stay calm. Playing something down is not by itself proof of lying; this entry documents the gap between his private remarks and public messaging.

title: The wall: 'I will have Mexico pay' vs 'I didn't say they're going to write me a check'

before.quote: And I will have Mexico pay for that wall. Mark my words.
before.where: Presidential campaign announcement speech

after.quote: I didn't say they're going to write me a check for $20 billion or $10 billion.
after.where: Border roundtable, McAllen, Texas

context: PolitiFact rated the 2019 claim False: Trump's own campaign memo called a one-time payment of $5 billion to $10 billion 'an easy decision for Mexico,' contradicting the claim that he never meant a check. Trump later argued Mexico pays indirectly through a trade deal; the Associated Press found that deal contains no such payment (see the separate entry).
